title: Final temperature in A
description: Essential: The final answer must be the correct temperature of the gas in tube A, approximately 387.7 K or 114.7°C.

title: Initial pressure in B
description: Important: The student must correctly calculate the initial pressure of the gas in tube B as p0 + Δh = 80 cmHg.

title: Mercury level changes
description: Important: The student must apply fluid volume conservation to relate the level changes Δh1 and Δh2 in tubes A and B, solving for their values (e.g., Δh1 = 3 cm).

title: Final pressure in A
description: Important: The student must correctly determine the final pressure in tube A by considering the equal liquid levels and the isothermal process in B to find the new pressure in B.

title: Ideal gas law application
description: Important: The student must correctly apply the ideal gas law to the sealed gas in tube A, using initial and final pressures/volumes to solve for the final temperature.

title: Area ratio consideration
description: Important: The student must correctly incorporate the 3:1 cross-sectional area ratio between tubes B and A in volume and fluid displacement calculations.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The student's work should maintain consistent units (e.g., cmHg for pressure, cm for length, Kelvin for temperature).

title: Sign error in displacement
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student misassigns the direction of mercury level changes or incorrectly relates Δh1 and Δh2 to the initial height difference Δh.

title: Pressure equilibrium mistake
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student fails to establish that final pressures at the mercury interface are equal, or incorrectly equates gas pressures in A and B without accounting for the mercury column.
